summary: Configured Fleet Internal CA, issued and deployed node2’s certificate, enabled trusted HTTPS on port 8443, and verified persistence through sequential restarts of both CentOS 5 nodes.
actions_performed: Created the Fleet Internal CA on node1.
Generated node2’s private key locally and signed its CSR on node1.
Installed the CA into both system trust bundles.
Configured a non-root SysV-managed OpenSSL HTTPS service on node2.
Persistently allowed inbound TCP/8443 through node2’s firewall.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified recovery.

evidence.requirement: Create Fleet Internal CA on node1
evidence.summary: Shows the self-signed Fleet Internal CA with critical CA constraints and certificate-signing usage.

evidence.requirement: Issue a TLS certificate for node2
evidence.summary: The CSR verified, the signed certificate chains to Fleet Internal CA, contains node2 DNS/IP identities, and matches node2’s private key.

evidence.requirement: Install the CA as a trusted system authority on both nodes
evidence.summary: Both nodes validate the installed CA through their system trust configuration after restart.

evidence.requirement: Serve trusted HTTPS on node2 port 8443
evidence.summary: The enabled service listens on 8443; node1 receives HTTP 200 with subject node2, issuer Fleet Internal CA, and verification code 0.
Healthy baseline and boot ID 0e1d6b49…; restart acknowledged; new boot ID 552c6212…; CA, trust, and remote HTTPS validation recovered.
Healthy baseline and boot ID 0eeb400e…; restart acknowledged; new boot ID bca00e4b…; HTTPS service, listener, certificate, trust, firewall, and HTTP 200 recovered.

evidence.requirement: Keep installed OS release and kernel
evidence.summary: Both nodes remain on CentOS 5.11 with kernel 2.6.18-398.el5.
